overview: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, both in area and in population. It is completely surrounded by the city of Rome. It is the home of the Pope, who is the head of the Catholic Church and also the ruler of the country. Vatican City became an independent state in 1929.

geography.text: The whole country covers less than half a square kilometre, on a low hill on the west bank of the River Tiber. Much of it is taken up by St Peter's Basilica, St Peter's Square, the Vatican Museums and the Vatican Gardens, all enclosed by walls.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Mediterranean, like the rest of Rome: hot summers and mild winters.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: The Vatican Gardens are home to many birds, including parakeets now living wild in Rome.

history.text: For more than a thousand years, popes ruled the Papal States, a large territory across central Italy. When Italy was unified, it took Rome in 1870, and the popes refused to recognise the new Italian state. The dispute was settled by the Lateran Treaty of 1929, which created Vatican City as an independent country.

events.title: New St Peter's
events.text: Work begins on the new St Peter's Basilica.

events.title: Sistine Chapel ceiling
events.text: Michelangelo finishes painting the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.

events.title: Rome taken
events.text: Italian troops capture Rome, ending the Papal States.

events.title: Lateran Treaty
events.text: An agreement with Italy creates Vatican City.

events.title: Second Vatican Council
events.text: A major council begins modernising the Catholic Church.

government.text: Vatican City is ruled by the Pope, who holds full legislative, executive and judicial power. The Pope is elected for life by the cardinals of the Catholic Church in a secret meeting called a conclave. Day-to-day running of the city-state is handed to a commission. It is the smallest country in the world.

economy.text: The Vatican has no taxes and no ordinary businesses. Its money comes from donations from Catholics around the world, entry fees to the Vatican Museums, stamps and coins, and investments. It uses the euro and issues its own euro coins.

culture.text: Vatican City is the centre of the Catholic Church, which has more than a billion members. The Vatican Museums hold one of the world's greatest art collections, and Michelangelo painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel. Latin is still used in official documents.

items.title: Sistine Chapel
items.text: Its ceiling was painted by Michelangelo between 1508 and 1512.

items.title: St Peter's Basilica
items.text: One of the largest churches in the world.

items.title: Swiss Guard
items.text: The Pope's bodyguards since 1506, wearing striped uniforms.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: The Vatican has no national dish; food is the same as in Rome around it.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: The Vatican Museums hold one of the world's greatest art collections, including Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: When a new Pope is elected, white smoke rises from the Sistine Chapel chimney.

sport.text: The Vatican has no national football team in FIFA, but its staff play in a small football league. In 2019 the Vatican created its own athletics team, Athletica Vaticana, made up of priests, nuns and staff.

items.title: Athletica Vaticana
items.text: The Vatican's running team, founded in 2019.

items.title: Clericus Cup
items.text: A football tournament between teams of priests and seminarians in Rome.

didYouKnow: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, at about 0.44 km².
The Vatican has its own post office, newspaper and radio station.

keyPeople.name: Pope Francis
keyPeople.text: Led the Catholic Church from 2013 until his death in 2025, the first from the Americas.
